Condor Ferries: Motorcycling the Channel Islands

The Channel Islands sit tantalisingly close to the French coast yet belong to the British Crown. Getting there by motorcycle means Condor Ferries — the lifeline connecting Poole and Portsmouth to Guernsey and Jersey. Here's your complete guide.

Routes and Sailing Times

  • Poole to Guernsey: 3 hours (high-speed) or 7 hours (conventional). The high-speed Liberation catamaran is the flagship service.
  • Poole to Jersey: 4.5 hours (high-speed) or 10.5 hours (conventional via Guernsey).
  • Portsmouth to Guernsey: 7 hours (conventional Goodwill vessel, overnight sailings available).
  • Inter-island (Guernsey to Jersey): 1 hour (high-speed). Perfect for a day trip between islands.

Booking Your Motorcycle

Condor's booking system categorises motorcycles separately from cars:

  • Book online at condorferries.co.uk. Select "motorcycle" as your vehicle type.
  • Motorcycle fares are typically 40-50% of car fares — a significant saving.
  • Summer weekends (especially Friday outbound and Sunday return) book up fast. Secure your crossing 4-8 weeks in advance for July and August.
  • Midweek sailings are cheaper and less crowded — ideal if you have flexibility.
  • Check for motorcycle-specific promotions. Condor occasionally runs discounted biker weekends.

What to Expect at the Terminal

Arrive at least 90 minutes before your sailing — Condor is strict about check-in deadlines.

  • You'll check in at the vehicle lane and receive boarding instructions.
  • Motorcycles board via the car deck ramp.
  • On the high-speed vessel, bikes are strapped down by crew using wheel chocks and ratchet straps.
  • On the conventional vessel, you may be asked to use your side stand and leave the bike in gear.
  • Remove loose luggage — the vehicle deck is sealed during crossing.
Condor's crew handle motorcycles daily and are very professional. If your bike has a centre stand, mention it — they may prefer it for the crossing. Communication is key.

Riding in the Channel Islands

The Channel Islands are compact but rewarding for motorcyclists:

  • Guernsey: 25 square miles. Speed limit 35mph (25mph in many areas). Narrow lanes, stunning coastal cliffs, and a completely different pace of life.
  • Jersey: 45 square miles. Slightly faster roads, dramatic north coast cliffs, and beautiful bays on the south coast.
  • Both islands have their own vehicle requirements — no MOT is needed but your UK licence and insurance must be valid.
  • Fuel is slightly cheaper than the UK mainland.
  • Parking is generally easy for motorcycles, with many free motorcycle bays.

Costs (2026 Approximate)

  • Poole to Guernsey (high-speed): £80-130 return (motorcycle + rider)
  • Poole to Jersey (high-speed): £90-140 return
  • Inter-island (Guernsey-Jersey): £30-50 return
  • Portsmouth to Guernsey (conventional): £60-100 return

Planning Your Channel Islands Tour

A long weekend (3-4 days) is ideal for both islands. Here's a suggested itinerary:

  • Day 1: Ferry to Guernsey. Explore St Peter Port, coastal roads, and settle in.
  • Day 2: Circuit of Guernsey — south coast cliffs, west coast bays, German occupation bunkers.
  • Day 3: Ferry to Jersey for a day trip. North coast, St Brelade's Bay, Mont Orgueil Castle.
  • Day 4: Return ferry to Poole.

The Channel Islands offer a taste of European touring without leaving the Crown Dependencies. The combination of the ferry journey, island riding, and the relaxed pace of life makes this a unique UK touring experience. faq.q: How much do Condor motorcycle fares cost?
faq.a: Motorcycle fares are typically 40 to 50% of car fares, a significant saving. Approximate return prices for a motorcycle and rider are £80 to £130 Poole to Guernsey by high-speed craft, £90 to £140 Poole to Jersey, £30 to £50 for the inter-island hop, and £60 to £100 Portsmouth to Guernsey on the conventional vessel.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: Summer weekends, especially Friday outbound and Sunday return, book up fast, so secure your crossing four to eight weeks in advance for July and August. Midweek sailings are cheaper and less crowded if you have flexibility, and Condor occasionally runs discounted biker weekends worth watching for.

faq.q: When should I arrive at the terminal?
faq.a: Arrive at least 90 minutes before your sailing, because Condor is strict about check-in deadlines. You check in at the vehicle lane, board via the car deck ramp, and on the high-speed vessel crew strap the bike down with wheel chocks and ratchet straps. Remove loose luggage, as the vehicle deck is sealed during the crossing.

faq.q: What are the roads like in the Channel Islands?
faq.a: Guernsey covers 25 square miles with a 35mph limit (25mph in many areas), narrow lanes and stunning coastal cliffs. Jersey is 45 square miles with slightly faster roads, dramatic north coast cliffs and beautiful southern bays. No MOT is needed but your UK licence and insurance must be valid, and fuel is slightly cheaper than the mainland.

faq.q: How long do I need for both islands?
faq.a: A long weekend of three to four days suits both. A typical plan is a ferry to Guernsey and St Peter Port on day one, a circuit of Guernsey's cliffs, bays and occupation bunkers on day two, an inter-island ferry to Jersey for its north coast and Mont Orgueil Castle on day three, and the return ferry to Poole on day four.
